question: Should a recording get its zooms from your clicks with one command, the way Screen Studio does?
context: Photonz already records every click and can zoom to frame a spot. Screen Studio's best-known trick is making those zooms for you from the clicks. This asks whether Photonz should do the same, and how.

options.label: Add Zooms from Clicks, one command
options.summary: Clip menu and the clip's right-click get Add Zooms from Clicks. It puts a zoom on each burst of clicks in the recording, easing in just before and out just after. You then move, trim or delete them like any zoom you drew.
pros: A raw recording looks polished in one step, which is what people pick Screen Studio for
The zooms are ordinary ones you already know how to adjust
Nothing appears until you ask for it
cons: One more row in the Clip menu and the right-click
A busy recording can get more zooms than you want and you delete the extras
options.mitigation: Clicks close together share one zoom, and one Undo removes all of them.

options.label: Zooms appear by themselves on opening
options.summary: When a recording with clicks opens, its zooms are already there, as in Screen Studio. A switch in the clip's settings turns them off.
pros: No step at all: the first playback already zooms
cons: Opening a recording changes it before you have done anything
Every recording you open for a plain trim zooms, and you have to turn it off
options.mitigation: Only recordings made in Photonz with clicks get them, and the switch remembers your last choice.

options.label: Do not build this
options.summary: Zooms stay something you make by hand, one at a time.
pros: Nothing new to learn or tidy up
cons: Polishing a recording stays slower than in Screen Studio
options.mitigation: Drawing a zoom by hand already follows the pointer.
